Summary of Curve Sketching

The A–H checklist: domain, intercepts, symmetry, asymptotes, f′ and f″, then draw.

0 / 6 problems mastered

§4.5 puts everything together. Homework #7–53 all say “use the guidelines to sketch the curve”. On a quiz you will be graded on the list of facts as much as the drawing, so write each step down.

  1. Domain
  2. Intercepts: yyy-int f(0)f(0)f(0); xxx-ints where f=0f=0f=0
  3. Symmetry: even f(−x)=f(x)f(-x)=f(x)f(−x)=f(x), odd f(−x)=−f(x)f(-x)=-f(x)f(−x)=−f(x), periodic
  4. Asymptotes: vertical (denominator 0), horizontal (lim⁡x→±∞\lim_{x\to\pm\infty}limx→±∞​), slant (long division)
  5. Increasing/decreasing from f′f'f′
  6. Local max/min
  7. Concavity and inflection points from f′′f''f′′
  8. Sketch using all of the above
Vertical asymptote

x=ax=ax=a where the denominator is 0 (and the top isn't). Check lim⁡x→a±\lim_{x\to a^\pm}limx→a±​ to see which way it goes.

Horizontal asymptote

y=Ly=Ly=L if lim⁡x→∞f=L\lim_{x\to\infty}f=Llimx→∞​f=L or lim⁡x→−∞f=L\lim_{x\to-\infty}f=Llimx→−∞​f=L. For rational functions compare the degrees.

Slant asymptote

When the top's degree is exactly one more than the bottom's, long-divide: f=mx+b+rembottomf=mx+b+\frac{\text{rem}}{\text{bottom}}f=mx+b+bottomrem​. The line y=mx+by=mx+by=mx+b is the asymptote.

Traps

Inflection point at an asymptote

Concavity can flip at a vertical asymptote (like ex/xe^x/xex/x at x=0x=0x=0), but that's not an inflection point: the function isn't defined there.

Skipping the limits at the VA

Find which side goes to +∞+\infty+∞ and which to −∞-\infty−∞. It decides how the sketch looks.
